A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DOGE research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D are readable and support reliable matching of retained, relocated, and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original vision and GLUE experiments, component ablations, unseen-task evaluations, corruption tests, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds generative-language evaluations, larger task collections, coefficient sensitivity results, and another unseen-task experiment.

M1.justification: The loss-gap objective, modification vector, orthogonal gradient projection, and norm-based merging coefficients remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 now includes the second SVD already described in v1 Section 4.2. Newly stated pruning and linear-layer restrictions disclose implementation details without establishing a change to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained eight vision datasets and eight GLUE tasks, v3 adds twelve vision datasets for 14- and 20-task merging, including CIFAR100, PCAM, and RenderedSST2. Table 10 adds instruction-following, mathematics, and code-generation evaluations on AlpacaEval, GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval, and MBPP.

E2.justification: Original comparison sets are retained. v3 adds TA + DARE and TIES + DARE in Table 10, explicitly compares Consensus TIES and weight averaging in the vision scaling study, and adds quantitative resource/performance comparisons with EMR merging, Twin merging, and WEMoE in Table 15.

E3.justification: Added evaluations merge three 13B experts and report scores normalized to individual models, introduce a five-seen/three-unseen task design, and sweep eta from 0.01 to 0.09. Figure 3 switches the inspected MLP layer from the eleventh to the seventh. Existing benchmark training budgets and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds global-coefficient sensitivity analysis, transfer to three harder held-out tasks, scaling tests through 20 tasks, and analysis of static versus dynamic merging tradeoffs. These substantially extend the questions investigated. Original component, subspace-rank, corruption, and two-unseen-task analyses remain.

E5.justification: Figure 1 retains its 95% confidence intervals. Neither version specifies seeds or repeated-run counts, and the added evaluations introduce no uncertainty estimates or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in v1's ten tables are retained after matching relocated tables. Substantial new results appear: Table 10 reports a 90.0 normalized average versus 87.2 for TIES + DARE; Table 14 reports 20-task DOGE accuracies of 72.5 and 81.0. Table 12's unseen-task average is 51.5, below the pre-trained model's 55.6.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 adds an explicit linear-regime/NTK assumption and derives the gradient proxy from accumulated fine-tuning updates, obtaining the initial gradient as the negative task vector divided by summed learning rates. v1 supplied only the accumulated-gradient intuition. The central optimization equations remain equivalent; no new theorem or appendix proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: constrained model merging, a data-free objective, shared-subspace gradient projection, adaptive coefficients, and broad empirical effectiveness. Added evaluations support these existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v3 adds focused interpretations of coefficient stability and difficult unseen-task transfer, discusses storage, routing, and data tradeoffs against dynamic merging, and explicitly identifies heterogeneous model shapes or layer counts as an unaddressed limitation. The original conflict-resolution and shared-knowledge explanations remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies zero initialization of the modification vector, retention of the largest-magnitude 30% of parameters, and application only to linear layers. It also reports a 58-minute 13B merging run on one A100. Existing optimizer settings, software versions, and code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning against MAP, MetaGPT, TATR, TSV, and KnOTS, discussing prior loss-gap formulations and subspace merging. Section 4.1 now explicitly attributes the objective to Zhou et al. rather than presenting it without that attribution. Dynamic merging receives a new substantive comparison.

P1.justification: The overall section sequence and most prose remain. Changes include rewritten related-work paragraphs, expanded dataset descriptions, clearer methodological explanations, a revised conclusion, relocation of computational discussion into the main text, and updated author, affiliation, and acknowledgment information.

P2.justification: Five new tables substantially expand the experimental presentation. The original computational table moves from Appendix D to the main text, while existing tables are redistributed. Figure 2's projection legend is corrected, and Figure 3 is replaced with a larger seventh-layer distribution plot using a different vertical scale.

improvement.justification: The 13B instruction/math/code evaluations and 14-/20-task stress tests address important gaps in v1's evidence for scalability beyond eight-task vision and GLUE. Added sensitivity analysis, implementation disclosures, prior-work attribution, and an explicit architectural limitation improve support and assessability. Reporting remains imperfect—for example, Table 15's 81.0 with a +11.6 annotation is inconsistent with its 69.1 baseline—but these localized issues do not outweigh the substantial gains.
